question: Which brigade were the Washington, Idaho, 14th Infantry and 4th Cavalry in on 4-5 Feb?
what the sources say: S66 (January 1899): King = 4th Cav, 14th Inf, 1st California; Ovenshine = 1st Washington, 1st Idaho, 1st North Dakota. | S65 (5 Feb): King's swing was made by "the Californias, Washingtons and Idahos"; Ovenshine's line was "First North Dakota, 14th Infantry and 4th Cavalry".
how the pilot handled it: Assignments follow the roster until 3 Feb and Otis from 4 Feb.
comment: The brigades were evidently reorganized between January and the battle. A general order of late January would settle it.

question: Where were the 1st Nebraska at the close of 5 Feb: the reservoir or the waterworks?
what the sources say: S65: Nebraskans and a Tennessee battalion "captured the powder house and Deposito"; Otis had wired "Waterworks must wait". | S64 index: 1st Neb. "Waterworks".
how the pilot handled it: El Deposito at the close of 5 Feb; the waterworks (pumping station) is later than this playback.

question: Which lines on the Signal Corps map are 4 Feb and which later?
what the sources say: S64 title: positions prior to the battle of 5 Feb and after the capture of Caloocan, 10 Feb. No legend found on the sheet. "Former ... outpost" labels; heavy double-dashed lines named for regiments match the index of final positions.
how the pilot handled it: "Former" labels = before the battle; named heavy lines = final, shown from the time Otis's report puts the line there on 5 Feb.

question: When was San Isidro retaken in the fall: 20 or 22 October?
what the sources say: S74 (Otis): "October 20, the day upon which General Lawton's troops had seized San Isidro". | S68 (pamphlet): "San Isidro was recaptured October 22".

question: When and from where did Aguinaldo leave: Tarlac on the night of the 13th, or already at Bayambang on the 12th?
what the sources say: S74 (Buencamino, captured 21 Nov): "Buencamino and Aguinaldo on night 13th" left Tarlac. | S68, printing MacArthur's 1900 report: a council at Bayambang "about November 12" and a decree "Given at Bayambang, November 12, 1899". | S74 (rumour, 8 Nov): "reported to have left Tarlac November 1 for Bayombong".
how the pilot handled it: Shown at Tarlac until the 12th and at Bayambang on the 13th; low confidence.

question: When did the Navy occupy Vigan: 24 or 26 November?
what the sources say: S74 (Otis): "Vigan, which place Navy occupied 24th instant". | S75 (Parker, on the spot, "Vigan, November 26 - 1 p. m."): "On the morning of this date war ships shelled trenches ... landed force of 200 and occupied this town".

question: When did Wheaton land at San Fabian: 7 or 9 November?
what the sources say: S74 (8 Nov): "Wheaton should have landed at San Fabian yesterday." | S74 (10 Nov): "He secured lodgment yesterday at San Fabian". | S68: 7 November.

question: When did Young's cavalry reach Tayug?
what the sources say: S74, S68: by 11-13 November. | S80 p. 148: San Jose on the 12th, Umingan on the 13th, then the cavalry to Tayug and San Nicolas.
status: Settled: Linn (S80) followed, at Morgan's choice (22 Nov 2026).

question: Where was Young on 16 November?

how the pilot handled it: Binalonan (LZ037) kept in the workbook but not drawn.

question: When did Young reach Cabanatuan?
what the sources say: S74: 30 October, Aliaga on the 31st. | S80 pp. 146-147: Santa Rosa on the 28th, a three-day halt, then Cabanatuan; Talavera and Aliaga later.

question: The first shot, 4 Feb: how many Filipinos did the picket fire on, and were they killed?
what the sources say: S65 (Otis, p. 161): "an insurgent approaching the picket and refusing to halt or answer when challenged"; "our picket discharged his piece". One man; Otis does not say he was hit. | S82 (Wolff, 1960): Grayson "shot and killed two Filipino soldiers".
how the pilot handled it: Otis followed: one Filipino soldier, with no word on whether he was hit. The picket is named Grayson on S82, which Otis does not contradict.
status: Settled: S65 followed, at Morgan's choice (22 Nov 2026).
